scientific.title: Radial height from the Cassini-derived Epimetheus shape model above the 58.2 km reference sphere. Includes the broad irregular figure; not a local geodetic DEM.

metadata.label: Monochrome
metadata.coverage: Cassini clear-filter observations projected onto the released PDS shape using its measured camera geometry. Bounded illumination correction and exposure matching reduce photographed lighting. Gray grid marks unavailable samples; cast-shadow terrain is not reconstructed.

celestial.sunSource: Vendored JPL Saturn satellite orbit and the Archinal rotation frame documented with the PDS shape model.

panel.introduction: Epimetheus shares an orbit with the larger moon Janus. The pair exchanges inner and outer tracks about every four years. Cassini revealed a battered icy surface, including a flattened south pole and branching ridges.

controls.label: Monochrome

controls.title: ISS mosaic
controls.summary: Brightness matching reduces photographed shading. The gray grid marks missing coverage and terrain hidden in cast shadows.

controls.label: Elevation
controls.description: Radial height above a 58.2 km reference sphere from the Cassini shape model. Includes the moon’s broad irregular shape; it is not local height above a geoid. Fixed relief lighting reveals model slopes. Small craters are not reliably resolved.
controls.title: Shape-derived radial height
controls.summary: Height relative to a 58.2 km sphere, from the Cassini shape model. Small craters are unresolved.

charts.alt: JWST/NIRSpec · 2022-11-08, 22:15–22:29 UT. Dither 1: disk-integrated flux density; bars show the released 1σ statistical errors. Negative samples and instrumental outliers are retained. Background and calibration systematics are not included in these errors. This measures light from the whole unresolved moon, not a spatial composition map. Shorter wavelengths were excluded by the authors because of ring stray light.
